cosy-lesson.title: Watching Too Much TV in Midlife May Shrink the Brain

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Midlife – the central period of a person's life, spanning from around 40 to 60.

p.em: Example: Establishing healthy exercising habits in midlife is vital for smooth aging.

cosy-blockquote.p: Shrinkage – the process of becoming smaller in size or volume.

p.em: Example: MRI scans showed noticeable tissue shrinkage in several vital brain areas.

cosy-blockquote.p: Atrophy – the wasting away of body tissue or an organ, especially the brain's gray matter.

p.em: Example: Muscle atrophy occurs rapidly when a patient stays in bed for weeks.

cosy-blockquote.p: Passive – tending to be inactive or receptive; not active.

p.em: Example: Watching TV is a passive activity, unlike playing chess or reading books.

cosy-blockquote.p: Volumetric – relating to the measurement of physical volume or size.

p.em: Example: The software provides a detailed volumetric analysis of internal organ structures.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive reserve – the brain's ability to improvise and find alternate ways of getting a job done.

p.em: Example: Learning a foreign language is a great way to build your cognitive reserve.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sedentary – tending to spend much time seated; physically inactive.

p.em: Example: Sitting on a couch for five hours every evening is a highly sedentary habit.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cortical – relating to the outer layer of the brain (the cortex).

p.em: Example: The cortical thickness of the brain is associated with overall intelligence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Deterioration – the process of becoming progressively worse.

p.em: Example: Smoking and poor nutrition lead to rapid physical deterioration in adults.

cosy-blockquote.p: Neurogenesis – the growth and development of nervous tissue or brain cells.

p.em: Example: Aerobic physical exercise is one of the few habits proven to stimulate neurogenesis.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, why is midlife described as a critical biological window for protecting brain volume?
※ How have your personal hobbies and free time interests changed since your teenage years?

What evidence presented in the study proves that television-viewing is associated with physical brain shrinkage?
※ Have you ever felt mentally exhausted or "foggy" after binge-watching a TV show?

How does the paper explain the difference between ordinary age-related brain changes and pathological gray matter atrophy?
※ Do you practice any memory exercises or brain training games regularly?

According to the researchers, why does a highly passive leisure activity like TV viewing provide zero stimulation for cerebral networks?
※ Do you prefer passive entertainment like movies or active entertainment like board games?

What volumetric MRI measurements were recorded when tracking the brains of heavy television viewers?
※ Would you get a volumetric brain scan to check your biological brain age if it was free?

According to the article, how does a rich cognitive reserve act as a buffer against neurological diseases?
※ What complex skills or languages do you hope to learn in the next few years?

How did the scientists control for other sedentary risk factors, such as sitting at a desk during work hours?
※ Do you stand up and stretch regularly when working long hours at a desk?

Based on the study, what specific regions of the cortical gray matter showed the fastest rate of tissue loss?
※ Do you consider yourself more of a logical, analytical thinker or an emotional, intuitive person?

What physical and mental symptoms are first associated with the progressive deterioration of the frontal cortex?
※ What is your biggest fear regarding growing older?

According to the paper, can physical exercise completely reverse TV-induced brain changes and stimulate healthy neurogenesis?
※ Does physical exercise make you feel more creative and mentally focused?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this hypothesis, public health guidelines will recommend limiting television watching in midlife to exactly 5 hours per week.
※ Could you limit your movie and series streaming to just 5 hours a week?

As our understanding of this scientific breakthrough develops, streaming services will be legally required to show warnings about brain shrinkage before allowing binge-watching.
※ Should Netflix have a warning like "Too much watching may shrink your brain"?

Imagine future research proves that atrophy of brain tissue can be fully stopped by replacing passive viewing with interactive virtual reality experiences.
※ Would you wear virtual reality glasses to watch interactive educational shows?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to monitor biological volumetric brain changes in real time through commercial sleep headbands.
※ Would you buy a sleeping headband that warns you if your brain is getting smaller?

If future research continues to support this discovery, we will find that building a strong cognitive reserve in middle age completely prevents Alzheimer's disease.
※ Do you think learning difficult skills is the best investment we can make for our older years?

As our understanding of this scientific breakthrough develops, we will prove that a highly sedentary childhood leads to much faster brain decline in middle age.
※ Should children be forced to do mandatory physical exercise after school hours?

Imagine future research shows that cortical thickness can be permanently maintained by playing strategy-based computer games instead of watching videos.
※ Do you think video games are actually healthier for the brain than television?

If future research continues to support this discovery, we will use acoustic stimulation during sleep to reverse TV-induced mental deterioration.
※ Would you play brain-boosting sounds in your bedroom while sleeping?

As our understanding of this scientific breakthrough develops, we will identify the exact genetic markers that trigger healthy neurogenesis in older adults.
※ If you could modify your genes to grow new brain cells forever, would you do it?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to generate a chemical compound that turns a passive TV show into a highly active mental training session.
※ Would you take a pill that forces your brain to study while you relax and watch a cartoon?

ul.li: Incorrect: Watching too much TV leads to shrink the brain. → Correct: Watching too much TV leads to brain shrinkage / shrinks the brain. ((Underlined error: 'leads to' should be followed by a noun or gerund 'shrinking', not base infinitive))
Incorrect: We need to keep our brains active as we get older. → Correct: We need to keep our brains active as we get older. ((This is correct! Good usage of 'as' to describe a progression of time))
Incorrect: This results with a brain decline. → Correct: This results in brain decline. ((Underlined prepositional error. Correct collocation: 'result in'))
